text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division this weekend.

Fortuna Duesseldorf (16) v Karlsruhe (7). This should be competitive since Fortuna need points to get out of the relegation zone and Karlsruhe are still in with an outside chance of a place in Europe next season.

Hansa Rostock (13) v Bayern Munich (1). Perhaps the most important game of the season for Bayern after a week of more controversy in their camp. A defeat and their championship hopes may be in real danger of disappearing. Veteran libero Lothar Matthaeus will miss the game because of thigh strain. Hansa need points to stay well clear of the relegation zone.

Borussia Moenchengladbach (11) v Bochum (5). Newly-promoted Bochum have been the one of the biggest surprises of the season and now look well-placed to get a place in the UEFA Cup next season. But they are sure to find it hard to get points at Moenchengladbach who are much improved.

Bayer Leverkusen (2) v St. Pauli (17). Leverkusen have looked very strong in recent weeks and struggling St. Pauli seem there for the taking. A victory and this could be the weekend when Leverkusen take charge of the title race.

Borussia Dortmund (4) v Werder Bremen (8). European Cup finalists Dortmund now look out of the title race and are unlikely to even make the Champions League by finishing second. Victory in the European Cup final in Munich later this month seems their only path to Europe's most lucrative competition next year. Three points against Bremen will help their confidence, however.

1860 Munich (6) v Schalke (10). Schalke are sure to have their minds on next week's UEFA Cup final second leg at Internazionale Milan but the home team, who are still in running for place in Europe next season, will not provide an easy warm-up match.
VfB Stuttgart (3) v Duisburg (15). Both teams have different priorities at the top and bottom of the table respectively. This will be very competitive.
Hamburg (14) v Cologne (12). Hamburg and Cologne should both avoid relegation but they both need to get three points from a game like this to get away from the zone.

Freiburg (18) v Arminia Bielefeld (9). Promoted Bielefeld are sure of football in the top flight next season. Freiburg are doomed to second division football but clinched a goalless draw at Bayern last week. Freiburg have nothing to lose and could be dangerous in their last few games.
